page: Amazon Web Services i8g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 physical cores (64 vCPUs) running on an AWS-manufactured arm64 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core and dedicated allocation. Memory capacity sits at 512.0 GB (8.0 GB per core), paired with 36 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1d cache. Bundled hardware storage provides 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps and operates without dedicated discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight extreme multi-core throughput and superior memory bandwidth across dense parallel workloads. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,917.0 and high multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 651.08 GB/sec. Memory performance reaches the top 10% tier with 463.28 GB/sec for large block read-only bandwidth and 215.29 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-level benchmarks, it executes 132.34 million Redis SET operations per second and records 124.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1894.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1706.79, fall within average percentiles.

The dense pairing of 15 TB NVMe storage, 512 GB RAM, and high multi-threaded throughput delivers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy data infrastructure, reducing the footprint needed for clustered storage workloads. Potential tradeoffs stem from moderate single-core speeds and the lack of x86-specific vector extensions like AVX-512, which may impact legacy binaries not optimized for arm64. The instance is suited for large-scale transactional and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching systems, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput static web distribution.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.16xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured without multi-threading across its 64 vCPUs, it features 512.0 GB of memory and 15,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional multi-core performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,917.0, a PassMark database score of 47,372.78, and over 132 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core computational speeds remain average, its substantial memory bandwidth and raw NVMe capacity deliver high efficiency for storage-dense architectures. This instance is best suited for large distributed databases, in-memory key-value stores, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
